sampling_model.design: Independent uniform complete randomization on \(B\) and \(S\), with exactly \(n_B\) treated buyers and \(n_S\) treated sellers.
sampling_model.units: The finite populations \(B\) and \(S\) and all dyad potential outcomes are fixed; assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: A dyad has exposure \((z_i^B,z_j^S)\in\{0,1\}^2\); the tested contrast compares \((1,1)\) with \((0,0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No superpopulation overlap condition is used; positivity is the finite support condition \(h(a,b)\ge R\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The procedure enumerates or exactly samples the conditional randomization law.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 establishes that Procedure 3.2 is valid for any block size \(k\).
The randomization test described in Procedure 1 is valid conditionally at any level.
If \(T\) is imputable, the randomization test is valid at any level \(\alpha\).
Then, \(W\) is uniformly distributed conditional on the event \(\{W\in\mathcal B\}\).
If \(T\) is effect increasing, then \(p^{L+}(D^{\mathrm{obs}},\theta)\) is non-decreasing in \(\theta\).
The concentration probability is maximized when all the \(a_i\) are \(\pm1\).

body.tldr: Independent half-randomization on two market sides creates many exact conditional tests, but no rule currently identifies the covering rectangle that retains the most dyads at a required randomization resolution. The central result reduces this margin-sized combinatorial optimization to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\), proves every optimizer is captured uniformly over aspect ratios, and gives the exact affine phase envelope and all equality cases. A constant-incidence sampler implements every optimal event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield an exact one-sided confidence ray for a sharp constant total effect.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice heuristically; general biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but not an extremal classification of covering product slices.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles, a structure narrow enough for exact extremal analysis but rich enough to improve materially on equal blocks.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument first bounds the residual on the smaller side and then copies that residual to the larger side without losing support, producing a finite catalog, an exact phase formula, an implementable conditional law, and exact inversion.

body.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off; the present frontier strictly enlarges that design class and certifies its optimum. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, which informs the objective but does not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) supply the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) supply the orbit-equivariance template, while the unequal rectangular sampler requires a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) supply discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here only after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are proved. Singhal (2019) supplies the bilinear subset-sum profile and purification viewpoint, but not a coupled fixed-cardinality common-fiber extremum. Ye et al. (2023) provide the concrete unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The conditioning event must be selected without outcomes. Raw focal outcomes are not imputable under a nonzero sharp constant effect; the null-adjusted array \(Q_\tau\) is essential. Complement symmetry also implies that an ordinary nonrandomized absolute-score test has minimum \(p\)-value at least \(2/h(a,b)\), so support \(20\) cannot support an ordinary two-sided test at level \(0.05\).
body.honest_scope: The finite-catalog theorem, affine envelope, sampler, and one-sided sharp-null inversion are to be proved. Universal unit residuals remain an explicit open-ended question. The proposal makes no claim about weak-null validity, power optimality, confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, a minimal \(4R\) threshold, or the validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O. For the standard check \(R=4\), the frontier reduces to the stated four-block formula and unique paired multiset.
